subject.title: Session transcript doomloop: crash-restart cycle inflates transcript until gateway OOMs

question: What default recovery behavior should OpenClaw use when an active session transcript is too large or repeatedly crashes during gateway restart?
rationale: Automation can identify the unsafe whole-file load path, but choosing between quarantine/skip, truncation/reset, media dedupe, and doctor-guided recovery changes user-data preservation and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Pre-open quarantine with recovery
options.body: Detect oversized or repeatedly failing transcripts before whole-file repair/open, mark the session degraded, skip the crash loop, and expose a doctor/fix recovery path.

options.title: Automatic truncation or reset
options.body: Keep the gateway running by rewriting the active transcript automatically, accepting a higher risk of surprising transcript loss.

options.title: Bootstrap cap only
options.body: Land only the marker append circuit breaker as a partial mitigation while leaving the oversized transcript loader and recovery policy unresolved.

recommendation.title: Pre-open quarantine with recovery
recommendation.body: Detect oversized or repeatedly failing transcripts before whole-file repair/open, mark the session degraded, skip the crash loop, and expose a doctor/fix recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent, directly relevant embedded-runner/bootstrap/session history and are a plausible routing owner for the recovery-policy decision.
